rewrite.instruction: Continue the same afternoon from ch3's call: drive the firebreak ruts to the Mora factory, confront the Lisbon creditor, season saved. No dawn walk, no re-accusing Joaquim, no re-explaining the typo. 59 planks at the factory; the only thin plank is in Rosaria's kerchief. Keep her counting ending.

notes: Fixed year-digit maths (7 = 2017, story set 2026) and the typo mechanism across ch1-3, Joaquim's forty years, the phantom factory plank; ch4 rewritten to stop replaying earlier scenes. Left 'one plank per tree' shorthand.

replace.with:
Wanjiru stared. He was right. Six prints were big and flat, just like Mr Barasa's shoes.

"I stand up there every morning to open the high window," said Mr Barasa. "Three mornings this week."

Two feet, three times. Six. But one print was tiny, like for a very small shoe.

replace.find: "Pick it up," he said. "It feels heavy. Violins should be light. I held one for four seconds last term. This is heavier."
replace.with: "Look inside," he said. "Violins ring when you tap them. I tapped one for four seconds last term. It rang like a little bell. This one goes thud."

replace.with: Very gently, with two fingers, he pulled at the little holes. Out came a red hair ribbon. Then a crumpled handkerchief. But no bow.

replace.with: Mr Barasa reached up to the top of the cupboard and lifted down the bow. Not one hair was broken. "Next time, ask a grown-up to reach high things," he said. "Benches are for sitting." Then he smiled wide and fixed his bow tie.
